summary: A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, journalists and residents said, as the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said they intercepted two cruise missiles fired by the Iran-backed militia. In Gaza, the Israeli military launched a rare ground operation in a Hamas-controlled area, leading dozens of families to flee their tents and shelters. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

title: Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
summary: The Israeli parliament on Tuesday elected as new speaker an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Matan Kahana, a former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of the agenda of Netanyahu.

title: Major setbacks for Netanyahu ahead of vote to name new Knesset speaker
summary: Since suffering heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party has repeatedly claimed the vote was “stolen” by Arab-led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. Those claims appear to be crumbling as he tries to cling to power, as the Israeli parliament is set to select a new speaker opposed to him. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

title: Breaking taboos: Egypt's sexual revolution takes to social media
summary: In Egypt, a sexual revolution is quietly unfolding on social media. Accounts followed by tens of thousands of people, with posts attracting millions of views, are tackling a wide range of issues surrounding sexuality – from the widespread practice of female genital mutilation (which 93 per cent of women in rural areas have undergone) to sex education and sexual pleasure.

title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu ‘cannot remain’ after alleged election interference by aide
summary: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. The former army chief called Netanyahu and his entourage an "immediate threat to democracy", hours after representatives discussed forming a national unity government.

title: Turkey and Qatar pledge unified stance against attacks in mutual defence pact
summary: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, the two leaders said in a joint statement. The defence pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.

title: Israel to ban far-left French politician Jean-Luc Mélenchon from entry
summary: The Israeli government said Thursday that it would ban far-left French leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon from entering the country after the French presidential contender said he would use French vessels to force aid into Gaza if he were elected. The announcement comes a day after France confirmed it had refused entry to the head of a body representing settlements in the occupied West Bank.

title: Israel kills six in Gaza hospital strike as 9-month-old baby freezes to death
summary: An overnight Israeli air strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza killed at least six Palestinians Thursday, including a teenage boy and a surgeon, medics said. Elsewhere in the devastated Palestinian territory, a nine-month-old baby died from the cold as families flee worsening flooding.

title: How FRANCE 24 traced Tehran-backed Afghan fighters from Syria to southeastern Iran
summary: Members of the Tehran-backed Afghan Shia militia known as the Fatemiyoun division have resurfaced in Iran after largely disappearing from public view following the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government in Syria in 2024. FRANCE 24 used "martyrdom” announcements and the geolocation of videos shared on social media to trace their presence.

title: "Er hat mir alles beigebracht": Bruno Mars trauert um seinen Vater
summary: Mit einem herzzerreißenden Foto nimmt Bruno Mars Abschied von seinem Vater. Es zeigt den Megastar, wie er den 74-Jährigen im Krankenhausbett umarmt. Das Bild entstand kurz vor dem Tod von Peter Hernandez, dem "besten Vater der Welt", wie Mars erklärt.

title: "Meine Hand ist ausgestreckt": Oliver Pocher macht Christian Düren ein Friedensangebot

title: Bruder des "King of Pop": Marlon Jackson hat Krebs

title: 264 Euro für Geschenke: Geld sitzt bei Deutschen zu Weihnachten trotz Krisen lockerer

title: Wie Training für den Kopf: Vorlesen fördert Sprachentwicklung, Lesen die des Gehirns

Bundesumweltminister Schneider wertet den Gipfel dennoch bereits als Erfolg.

title: Home Office tells woman born and raised in London she is not British
summary: Woman, 24, says she cannot work and faces destitution after it was discovered her mother had no right to UK passport A 24-year-old woman who was born and raised in London believing she was a British citizen has been left in a state of shock after being told by authorities that she is not British . title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
summary: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib , during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. title: France awaits verdict in landmark police brutality trial over Michel Zecler assault
summary: A French prosecutor on Thursday urged a court to jail three policemen who beat up a black music producer to four to six years, in a rare case of alleged police brutality to go to criminal court. The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered renewed outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic but authorities and law enforcement unions claim is limited to isolated cases. The prosecutor argued the case had caused "immense harm to Michel Zecler but also to society as a whole," and that those on trial had "betrayed" their uniform.

title: Rare EU-UK summit as Andy Burnham seeks to mend Brexit damage
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials were set to announce deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit Friday, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit. But in a potential spoiler for Burnham's "reset", Brussels said the deals coming into force would be conditional on reaching an agreement to cut university fees for EU students in Britain. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi tells us more.

title: 'Coalition of the Willing': Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin after Trump-Putin-Xi talks

The meeting – co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain – was being held shortly after unprecedented three-way talks in China between US President Donald Trump, Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping.

summary: Spain's Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged making "mistakes" as he faced off with his main conservative rival in a key debate on Thursday before an election next week that could leave the far right on the cusp of power. summary: Iraq has reached ​a compromise with the powerful Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah, three senior security officials said, after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi readied security forces to move against the group. Iraqi officials had accused the group of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions ​of dollars' worth of ‌state-owned oil. Under the deal brokered by senior Shi'ite political leaders to avert a confrontation, government ⁠forces were expected to move into the group's stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday.

title: Outcry as fossil fuels scrubbed from draft UN climate deal
summary: UN climate talks co-host Australia unveiled a new draft agreement Thursday that drops any mention of fossil fuels, the leading driver of global warming, sparking anger from campaign groups. The nearly 200 nations involved in the COP31 global climate talks in Turkey have until Friday to strike a final agreement, though the marathon negotiations often run into overtime. The summit is unfolding against a record-breaking El Nino, disasters fuelled by climate change from Europe to Nepal and a global energy shock triggered by the Iran war.
